walkthroughs.body_html:
Geographic Perspectives: Global Change — a core area of Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Geographic Perspectives: Global Change brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Geographic Perspectives: Global Change.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many planetary boundaries did Rockstrom et al identify in 2009?
What causes global sea level rise?
options: Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Sea level rises mainly because Arctic sea ice is melting.
Two main factors: thermal expansion of warming seawater, and the melting of land-based ice (glaciers and ice sheets) adding water to oceans.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between qualitative and quantitative data?
options: Qualitative data means high-quality data and quantitative means a lot of data.
Quantitative data is always more scientific and reliable than qualitative.
Quantitative data is numerical and measurable (traffic counts, river width); qualitative data is descriptive and non-numerical (interview quotes, photo descriptions, field sketches).
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
